## Condensate repair by parent-vapour borrow (`limiter`) {#sec-ch10-borrow}

Local symbols: $\mathcal P_c$ is the set of parent vapours of condensate $c$. Tracked in ISSUES.md.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Fills a negative condensate density from its parent vapours in the same cell, split by stoichiometric
mass, then sets the condensate to exactly zero; @eq-ch10-borrow-split.

**Data.** In and out: the species partial densities [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$] of every cell, ghosts included; the
parent shares are cached when the equation of state is built.

**Placement.** Inside every call of the conserved limiter, before the column repair: every stage and once more
before the saturation adjustment.

**Activation.** EOS `limiter: true`; default false. Only condensates that a nucleation reaction produces.

**Guarantee / limits.** Mass and every element conserved cell by cell; $E$ is not corrected; a deficit larger than
the parents' vapour is left to the column repair.

**Evidence.** `test_condensate_conservation` ($10^{-12}$; $10^{-6}$) and `borrow_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C4]`; the
ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

A negative condensate density means the positivity-limited transport over-drained a cell: the mass is in a
neighbour, not missing. Clamping it to zero would create mass one way; the borrow instead takes the deficit
from the vapours the condensate is made of, in the same cell, in the proportions of the reaction that makes it.
A cell whose vapour cannot cover the deficit goes vapour-negative and is handled by the column repair that follows
(@sec-ch10-fixvapor). The borrow runs inside every call of the conserved limiter, so on every stage and once more
before the saturation adjustment (@sec-ch10-satadj).

It is on with `limiter: true` and acts only on condensates that some nucleation reaction produces; a condensate
with no such reaction (rain, for example) is repaired by the column repair instead.

### Derivation

Let $c\in\mathcal C$ be a condensate and $k$ the first nucleation reaction listed with $c$ among its products.
Its parents $\mathcal P_c$ are the reactant vapours of $k$, dry air excluded. With $\lvert\nu_{mk}\rvert$ the
reactant coefficient of $m$ in $k$ and $\mu_m$ its molar mass, every cell applies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_m &\leftarrow \rho_m + \frac{\lvert\nu_{mk}\rvert\,\mu_m}{\sum_{m'\in\mathcal P_c}\lvert\nu_{m'k}\rvert\,\mu_{m'}}\,\min(\rho_c,0),\\
\rho_c &\leftarrow \max(\rho_c,0)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch10-borrow-split}

for every $m\in\mathcal P_c$. @eq-ch10-borrow-split is applied to the `deficit` in `apply_conserved_limiter_`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}), with the shares
normalised by `parent_mass` once, when the equation of state is built, in `cache_cloud_parents_`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}}).

The shares sum to one, so the parents lose exactly $-\min(\rho_c,0)$ and the condensate gains it: the cell's total
density is unchanged (`[C1]`).[^bor-c] Elements are conserved too. For $A+B\to AB$ the molar mass of the
condensate is $\mu_A+\mu_B$; filling a deficit $d$ fills $d/(\mu_A+\mu_B)$ moles of condensate and debits
$d\,\mu_A/(\mu_A+\mu_B)/\mu_A$ moles of $A$, the same number, and likewise for $B$ (`[C2]`, symbolic). Energy is not
corrected: $E$ is untouched, so the shift between phases moves the temperature through the reference energies by
the latent heat of the borrowed mass. The comment at the call site estimates the shift at about one per cent of the
local value and notes that the saturation adjustment re-equilibrates it within the same step; that estimate has no
measurement behind it here.

[^bor-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch10/borrow_check.py`, output `borrow_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C4]`; a
    numpy and sympy port of `cache_cloud_parents_` and of the borrow in `apply_conserved_limiter_` at the pin,
    double precision.

### Numerical method

The repair is pointwise in each cell and acts on the whole array, ghosts included, so a ghost copy receives the
identical repair and neighbouring ranks stay in step. It runs before the column repair, inside the same limiter
call. Two properties of the cache matter: only the first reaction that produces $c$ is read, and dry air is skipped
even if a card lists it as a reactant (`[C3]`, `[C4]`). The cache is built from the thermo's own copy of the species
names and molar masses, so a later card that refills kintera's global tables does not change it.
@fig-ch10-borrow-bars shows one cell.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-borrow-bars
#| fig-cap: "An $\\mathrm{NH_4SH(s)}$ deficit of $10^{-4}\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,m^{-3}}$ filled from $\\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\\mathrm{H_2S}$ in one cell. Sky-blue bars are the partial densities before the borrow, green hatched bars after it; the condensate ends at exactly zero and the two vapours lose one third and two thirds of the deficit, their molar-mass shares."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart of NH3, H2S and NH4SH(s) partial densities before and after; the negative NH4SH bar becomes zero, the vapour bars shrink."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.fig_borrow_bars import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| parent cache | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}} | `cache_cloud_parents_` | |
| dry slot never a parent | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}} | `vapor_it` | |
| first producing reaction | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}} | `break` | |
| borrow and clamp | {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} | `deficit` | `limiter` |

: Code map of the parent-vapour borrow. {#tbl-ch10-borrow-code}

1. When the equation of state is built, take the thermo's own names and molar masses, `populate_thermo`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}}).
2. Refuse a thermo whose tables disagree in length, `TORCH_CHECK`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}}).
3. Record the parents and their mass shares, `cloud_parent_cache_`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::cache_cloud_parents_ >}}).
4. In each limiter call, skip parentless clouds and borrow for the rest, `parentless`
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).

The only setup check is the table-length refusal of step 2, "[EquationOfState] thermo carries ... species names".

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_condensate_conservation.release` | total mass; molar-mass split | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-6}$ | test thresholds |
| `test_cloud_parent_slots.release` | parents with unused species | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-6}$ | test thresholds |
| `test_diffusion_moist.release` | limiter reads nucleation parents | $10^{-12}$; $10^{-6}$ | test thresholds |
| `test_two_cards_species.release` | split survives a second card | $10^{-10}$ (f64) | test threshold |

: Tests of the parent-vapour borrow; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run. {#tbl-ch10-borrow-tests}

`test_condensate_conservation` keeps the total mass to $10^{-12}$ and checks the $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{H_2S}$
debits against their molar-mass shares to $10^{-6}$, with the condensate exactly zero after
({{< code tests/test_condensate_conservation.cpp DeviceTest.multi_vapor_condensate_debits_stoichiometric_mass >}}).
The $10^{-6}$ of the share comparison is looser than the arithmetic; the source gives no reason for it, and
`borrow_check.py` `[C1]` shows the shares themselves are exact to round-off. The two-card test uses `tol` $=10^{-10}$ in
float64 and $10^{-4}$ in float32 ({{< code tests/test_two_cards_species.cpp expect_card_a_parents >}}).
All four run on CPU, and on CUDA where the device fixture is compiled; none is multi-rank. Measured results at the
pin are **missing evidence** (@sec-ch15-ch10-tests).

### Limits

- Only the first nucleation reaction that produces a condensate sets its parents; a second producing reaction is
  ignored (`borrow_check.py` `[C3]`).
- No energy correction: the borrowed mass changes phase at fixed $E$, so $T$ moves by the latent heat; the size of
  the move is not measured.
- A deficit larger than the parents' vapour leaves the vapour negative for the column repair; if the column cannot
  cover it, the vapour repair throws (@sec-ch10-fixvapor).
- Not in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).
